$comment: Example AuthorizationResponseEnvelope as it is signed by the beneficiary PSP (counterparty) on the auth_response path. Response-side mirror of PaymentRequestEnvelope/v1's example.json. The embedded VC uses the production-realistic `type: ["VerifiableCredential", "KnownToAtumVerifiableCredential"]` with the `known-to-atum/v1` context — the type-alias-to-IRI binding that makes canonicalization cross-language byte-identical. credentialSubject.role is `psp` (the beneficiary PSP is a payment service provider); a dedicated `beneficiaryPsp` role may be introduced in the issuer phase. proof.challenge is the authorization response hash — the content-addressed hash of the inner AuthorizationResponse this envelope accompanies ("0x"+keccak256 over the canonicalized, proof-stripped response), recomputed and asserted by the payment gateway; it is the response-side analog of the PaymentRequest's request_hash that PRE binds (NOT the PaymentRequest's request_hash itself). The value below is a PLACEHOLDER — the real challenge is derived from the specific inner AuthorizationResponse, which travels alongside this envelope and is not embedded here. proof.domain is the NETWORK-WIDE `did:web:atum.network` (same as PRE, NOT service-specific like FQE's). The proof JWS / proofValue below are PLACEHOLDERs (not real signatures) — re-sign with the canonical signer to produce a verifying example.
